Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

until preposition

up to a time

also till, up to, until evening, till late at night, to the end, till late in the day, till nightfall, until then, till then, up to that time, hitherto

classical

Cic. Amic. 33: ūsque ad extrēmum vītae diem
Cic. Fin. 1.72: ūsque ad senectūtem
Traupman 394, 400

1ūsque: long u (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan s.v. usque: the length is uncertain and Romance continues both; he takes shortening as likelier than lengthening, which speaks for the long vowel. The lexicon has both spellings so far.

ūsque ad + acc.1

adverb with the preposition ad and the accusative

until, right up to

For “until he came”, a clause with dum or dōnec.

Other words

  • ad + acc. — until, by (a time)

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 46: ad multam noctem; Cic. Att. 2.8.1: exspectārem ad vesperum

    ad vesperum, until evening; ad multam noctem, until late at night.

  • ad id tempus — until then, up to that time

    also used · classical · Caes. BC 1.24 (Lewis & Short s.v. ad); Sall. Jug. 63.6: ad id locōrum, to that time, till then (Lewis & Short s.v. locus); Traupman 88: at that time, ad id temporis

    Also ad id locōrum (Sallust, Livy). Traupman gives ad id temporis for “at that time”; with ad the phrase runs up to a limit, “until then”, and Lewis & Short quotes ad id tempus and ad id locōrum, not ad id temporis (for “at that time”, see then).

Examples

  • quamquam ille quidem nihil difficilius esse dīcēbat quam amīcitiam ūsque ad extrēmum vītae diem permanēre

    though he used to say that nothing was harder than for a friendship to last until one’s dying dayCic. Amic. 33

  • quae puerōs nōn didicisse turpe est, ea putant ūsque ad senectūtem esse discenda

    they think that what it is a shame for boys not to have learned must be studied until old ageCic. Fin. 1.72

  • convīviumque vīcīnōrum cotīdiē compleō, quod ad multam noctem quam maximē possumus variō sermōne prōdūcimus

    every day I fill my table with neighbours, and with talk of every kind we keep the party going as far as we can, until late at nightCic. Sen. 46

  • epistulam cum ā tē avidē exspectārem ad vesperum, ut soleō, ecce tibi nūntius puerōs vēnisse Rōmā!

    as I was eagerly waiting until evening for a letter from you, as I always do, look, word comes that the boys have arrived from Rome!Cic. Att. 2.8.1

  • quis est tam stultus, quamvīs sit adulēscēns, cui sit explōrātum sē ad vesperum esse vīctūrum?

    who is so foolish, however young, as to be sure he will live until evening?Cic. Sen. 67

  • hāc contrōversiā ūsque ad noctem ductā senātus dīmissus est

    this dispute dragged on until nightfall, and the senate was dismissedCic. Fam. 1.2.3

  • ad multum diem

    till late in the dayCic. Att. 13.9.1 (Lewis & Short s.v. multus); Traupman 86

  • in mēnsem Jūlium

    till the month of JulyTraupman 394

See also for, since, during, then.
